newsitem.title: USA: Compaq gross margins up, cash pile grows.
newsitem.headline: Compaq gross margins up, cash pile grows.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp said Wednesday its first quarter gross margins rose to 24.5 percent from 24.4 percent in the 1996 fourth quarter, and its cash pile grew to $4.7 billion.
Compaq reported first quarter earnings of $1.36 a share, up from $0.85 a year ago. The consensus estimate on Wall Street, according to First Call, was $1.31 a share.

Compaq said its continuing focus on asset management reduced its inventory by $666 million compared to the 1996 first quarter, leading to increased inventory turns and decreased sales outstanding and helping lift its cash balance.
Compaq ended the 1996 first quarter with $2.9 billion in cash and cash equivalents, and $1 billion in short-term investments. In the 1996 fourth quarter Compaq had a cash balance of $4 billion.
In the 1997 first quarter revenues grew 14.3 percent, to $4.8 billion from $4.2 billion a year earlier.

"We're very pleased with the consistency of our financial progress, especially with the improvements in earnings and the growth of gross margins to 24.5 percent," Eckhard Pfeiffer, president and CEO, said in a statement. "We expect strong growth throughout 1997."
"Compaq is positioned to gain market share and increase profits," Pfeiffer added. "We are clearly focused on what customers are looking for."
Compaq said it increased its inventory turns to 12.0 in the first quarter from 6.5 a year earlier, and cut its days of sales outstanding to 51 from 65.

Compaq said it is working with its computer reseller partners to fully implement a new manufacturing and delivery model that will create the most efficient fulfillment process for the lowest delivered cost in the industry. It said this will translate into lower prices for its customers.
